subject: START statement
notes: NOW (kb/Work PB3334, INDEXED on the keyed store engine): the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.4): START FIRST is the prime tree's first entry. kb/Work PB356 LANDED 2026-09-13. RULE: "If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the primary key of the first existing logical record in the physical file and the key of reference is set to the primary key. If no records exist in the file, the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to '23', the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful." (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the primary key of the first existing logical record in the physical file" -> OK 14.9.41.4 18); cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "the key of reference is set to the primary key" -> OK 14.9.41.4 18)). CODE: StartFirstLast now searches IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(PrimeKey) and completes through StartSucceeded(PrimeKey, rec) - a shared successful-START epilogue whose key of reference is a REQUIRED ARGUMENT, so no START format can leave the previous one standing. It no longer mentions _refKey at all: GR18 names the primary key twice, once as the ordering ("in the physical file") and once as the outcome. WAS: IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(_refKey) with no reset, justified by 14.9.27.4 GR14 - a real clause about what OPEN establishes, not about what START FIRST/LAST does. MEASURED before/after on a prime X(2) / alternate X(2) WITH DUPLICATES file whose two orderings are inverted (01/CC, 02/BB, 03/BB, 04/AA), with the ALTERNATE established as key of reference by a preceding START KEY IS EQUAL: START FIRST + READ NEXT gave PRIME=04 (the alternate's first), now gives PRIME=01; the three following READ NEXTs gave 02 with '02', 03, 01 (the alternate ordering, GR27's duplicate status), now give 02, 03, 04 all '00' - the key of reference really is the primary key for the subsequent sequential reads (GR16 last sentence; 14.9.30.4 GR21 b)). The SUPPRESS WHEN half is covered by conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb356_start_first_last_suppressed: with ALTERNATE ... SUPPRESS WHEN "ZZ" over records 01/ZZ, 02/MM, 03/ZZ, FIRST used to answer 02 and reach at-end after one read because IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(alt) had dropped the two suppressed records that 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 withholds from the ALTERNATE path ONLY; it now answers 01 and walks all three. The empty-file half was already correct and is pinned by the EF/EL arms of the 2002 golden (INVALID KEY + '23'). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: widened from 2014,2023 to 2002,2014,2023. The previous adjudication noted the 2023 transcription does not date the FIRST phrase's introduction; the compiler's own edition gate does - constructs.json start-first-last-2002 carries introducedIn 2002 with COBOL0900, and conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb352-start-sequential-first-below-2002 pins the rejection below it - so the rule's behaviour must hold at --std 2002, which the 2002 golden now exercises.
